nodes.name: Characteristic function
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a real inner product space $E$. The characteristic function of $\mu$, denoted by $\hat{\mu}$, is the function $E \to \mathbb{C}$ defined by \begin{align*} \hat{\mu}(t) = \int_x e^{i \langle t, x \rangle} d\mu(x) \: . \end{align*} The characteristic function of a random variable $X$ is defined as the characteristic function of $\mathcal L(X)$.
nodes.statement_short: Characteristic function $\hat\mu(t)=\int e^{i\langle t,x\rangle}d\mu(x)$ of a measure on a real inner product space; of a random variable via its law.
nodes.label: def:charFun

nodes.name: Characteristic function is bounded by 1
nodes.statement: For all $t$, $\Vert\hat{\mu}(t)\Vert \le 1$.
assumptions: For all $t$
nodes.label: lem:charFun_bounded

nodes.name: Smoothness of the characteristic function
nodes.statement: If $\mu[|X|^n] < \infty$ then the characteristic function of $\mu$ is continuously differentiable of order $n$.
assumptions: $\mu[|X|^n] < \infty$
conclusions: the characteristic function of $\mu$ is continuously differentiable of order $n$
nodes.label: lem:charFun_contDiff

nodes.name: Continuity of the characteristic function
nodes.statement: The characteristic function is a continuous function.
conclusions: The characteristic function is a continuous function.
nodes.label: lem:charFun_continuous

nodes.name: Characteristic function at -t
nodes.statement: $\hat{\mu}(-t) = \overline{\hat{\mu}(t)}$.
nodes.label: lem:charFun_neg

nodes.name: Characteristic function of a scalar multiple
nodes.statement: For $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and $X$ a random variable with law $\mu$, the characteristic function of $a X$ is $t \mapsto \hat{\mu}(at)$.
assumptions: $a \in \mathbb{R}$
$X$ a random variable with law $\mu$
conclusions: the characteristic function of $a X$ is $t \mapsto \hat{\mu}(at)$
nodes.label: lem:charFun_smul

nodes.name: Characteristic function of a sum of independent random variables
nodes.statement: If two random variables $X, Y : \Omega \to S$ with laws $\mu$ and $\nu$ are independent, then $X+Y$ has characteristic function $\hat{\mu} \times \hat{\nu}$.
assumptions: two random variables $X, Y : \Omega \to S$ with laws $\mu$ and $\nu$ are independent
nodes.label: lem:charFun_add_of_indep

nodes.name: Integral of exp(it) over [-r,r]
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \int_{-r}^r e^{i t} \, d t = 2 \sin r \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:integral_exp_I

nodes.name: Integral of the characteristic function
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \int_{-r}^r \hat{\mu}(t) dt = 2 r \int \frac{\sin(r x)}{r x} \, d\mu(x) \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:integral_charFun

nodes.name: Proof of LP8
nodes.statement: We will use Fubini's theorem to exchange the order of integration. \begin{align*} \int_{-r}^r \hat{\mu}(t) \, dt &= \int_{-r}^r \int e^{i t x} \, d\mu(x) \, dt \\ &= \int \left( \int_{-r}^r e^{i t x} \, dt \right) \, d\mu(x) \\ &= \int 2 \frac{\sin(r x)}{x} \, d\mu(x) \\ &= 2 r \int \frac{\sin(r x)}{r x} \, d\mu(x) \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Fubini's theorem to swap the integrals, then integrate $e^{itx}$ over $[-r,r]$.

nodes.name: Tail bound by the characteristic function
nodes.statement: For $\mu$ a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ and $r > 0$, \begin{align*} \mu \left\{x \mid |x| > r\right\} &\le \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - \hat{\mu}(t))dt \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Tail mass $\mu\{|x|>r\}$ is bounded by an integral of $1-\hat\mu$ over $[-2/r,2/r]$.
assumptions: $\mu$ a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$
nodes.label: lem:charFun_bound_large

nodes.name: Proof of LP9
nodes.statement: We will use Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_charFun} with $r$ replaced by $2/r$. \begin{align*} \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - \hat{\mu}(t))dt &= 2 - \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} \hat{\mu}(t)dt \\ &= 2 - 2 \int \frac{\sin(2 x / r)}{2 x / r} \, d\mu(x) \\ &= 2 \int \left(1 - \frac{\sin(2 x / r)}{2 x / r}\right) \, d\mu(x) \\ &\ge 2 \int_{|x| \ge r} \left(1 - \frac{\sin(2 x / r)}{2 x / r}\right) \, d\mu(x) \\ &\ge \mu\{x \mid |x| > r\} \: . \end{align*} In the end we used that $\sin x \le x /2$ for $x \ge 2$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the integral formula of Lemma 8 at $2/r$ and bound $1-\sin(y)/y$ from below on $|x|\ge r$.

nodes.name: Tail bound in a direction by the characteristic function
nodes.statement: For $\mu$ a probability measure on an inner product space $E$ and $r > 0$, $a \in E$, \begin{align*} \mu \left\{x \mid \vert\langle a, x\rangle\vert > r\right\} &\le \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - \hat{\mu}(t \cdot a))dt \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Mass of $\{|\langle a,x\rangle|>r\}$ is bounded by an integral of $1-\hat\mu(ta)$.
assumptions: $\mu$ a probability measure on an inner product space $E$
$a \in E$
nodes.label: lem:charFun_bound_inner

nodes.name: Convergence on exponential polynomials from convergence of characteristic functions
nodes.statement: Let $\mu, \mu_1, \mu_2, \ldots$ be probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with characteristic functions $\hat{\mu}, \hat{\mu}_1, \hat{\mu}_2, \ldots$ such that $\hat{\mu}_n \to \hat{\mu}$. Then for all exponential polynomial $f \in \mathcal M$, $\mu_n[f] \to \nu[f]$.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.origin_citation: Kallenberg (Foundations of Modern Probability); Bogachev (Measure Theory II); Ethier & Kurtz
assumptions: Let $\mu, \mu_1, \mu_2, \ldots$ be probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with characteristic functions $\hat{\mu}, \hat{\mu}_1, \hat{\mu}_2, \ldots$ such that $\hat{\mu}_n \to \hat{\mu}$.
nodes.label: lem:tendsto_M_of_tendsto_charFun

nodes.name: Measures are determined by their characteristic function
nodes.statement: Two finite measures on a complete separable metric space are equal iff they have the same characteristic function.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
assumptions: Two finite measures on a complete separable metric space
conclusions: Two finite measures on a complete separable metric space are equal iff they have the same characteristic function.
equivalent_conditions: they have the same characteristic function
nodes.label: lem:ext_charFun

nodes.name: Proof of LP12
nodes.statement: See Mathlib PR \#19783. The sub-algebra $\mathcal M$ of exponential polynomials is separating by Lemma~\ref{lem:separates_points_expPoly} and~\ref{thm:separating_starSubalgebra}. Equality of characteristic functions implies equality on $\mathcal M$, which then implies equality of the measures since $\mathcal M$ is separating.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Exponential polynomials form a separating star-subalgebra, and equal characteristic functions give equal integrals on it.

nodes.name: Tightness from pointwise convergence of characteristic functions
nodes.statement: Let $(\mu_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with characteristic functions $(\hat{\mu}_n)$. If $\hat{\mu}_n$ converges pointwise to a function $f$ which is continuous at 0, then $(\mu_n)$ is tight.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
assumptions: Let $(\mu_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with characteristic functions $(\hat{\mu}_n)$.
$\hat{\mu}_n$ converges pointwise to a function $f$ which is continuous at 0
nodes.label: lem:tight_of_tendsto_charFun

nodes.name: Proof of LP13
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:charFun_bound_inner} and dominated convergence, for all $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and $r > 0$, \begin{align*} \lim_{n \to +\infty} \mu_n \left\{x \mid |\langle a, x\rangle| \ge r\right\} &\le \lim_{n \to +\infty} \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - \hat{\mu}_n(\langle a, t\rangle))dt \\ &= \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - f(\langle a, t\rangle))dt \end{align*} The right-hand side converges to 0 as $r \to +\infty$ by continuity of $f$ at 0. This shows that the family is tight.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Bound directional tails by Lemma 10 and dominated convergence; continuity of the limit at 0 makes the bound vanish.

nodes.name: Tail bound
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:charFun_bound_inner} and dominated convergence, for all $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and $r > 0$, \begin{align*} \lim_{n \to +\infty} \mu_n \left\{x \mid |\langle a, x\rangle| \ge r\right\} &\le \lim_{n \to +\infty} \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - \hat{\mu}_n(\langle a, t\rangle))dt \\ &= \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - f(\langle a, t\rangle))dt \end{align*}
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Bound directional tail mass in the limit

nodes.name: Vanishing bound
nodes.statement: The right-hand side converges to 0 as $r \to +\infty$ by continuity of $f$ at 0.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Bound vanishes by continuity at 0

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: This shows that the family is tight.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Conclude tightness

nodes.name: Finite dimension is necessary for tightness
nodes.statement: Remark: the finite dimension is necessary. Counterexample: $\ell^2$ with $\mu_n$ the law of $X_n = \sum_{k=1}^n \zeta_k e_k$ where $e_k = (0, \ldots, 0, 1, 0 \ldots)$ and the $\zeta_k$ are i.i.d. $\mathcal N(0,1)$. Then $\hat{\mu}_n(t) \to e^{- \Vert t \Vert^2 / 2}$ for all $t \in \ell^2$ but $(\mu_n)$ is not tight.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: In $\ell^2$, laws of partial sums of i.i.d. Gaussian coordinates have converging characteristic functions yet are not tight.

nodes.name: Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement: Let $\mu, \mu_1, \mu_2, \ldots$ be probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with characteristic functions $\hat{\mu}, \hat{\mu}_1, \hat{\mu}_2, \ldots$. Then $\mu_n \xrightarrow{w} \mu$ iff for all $t$, $\hat{\mu}_n(t) \to \hat{\mu}(t)$.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Lévy's continuity theorem: weak convergence on $\mathbb{R}^d$ iff pointwise convergence of characteristic functions.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \mu_1, \mu_2, \ldots$ be probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with characteristic functions $\hat{\mu}, \hat{\mu}_1, \hat{\mu}_2, \ldots$.
nodes.label: thm:charFun_tendsto_iff_measure_tendsto

nodes.name: Proof of TP1
nodes.statement: For all $t$, $x \mapsto e^{i \langle t, x \rangle}$ is a bounded continuous function. Hence by the definition of convergence in distribution, $\mu_n \xrightarrow{w} \mu \implies \hat{\mu}_n(t) \to \hat{\mu}(t)$ for all $t$. Let's now prove the other direction. If the characteristic functions converge pointwise, we get from Lemma~\ref{lem:tight_of_tendsto_charFun} that the family of measures is tight. Then apply Lemma~\ref{lem:cvg_of_separating} to the subalgebra $\mathcal M$: it suffices to show that $\mu_n[f] \to \mu[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal M$. This is obtained with Lemma~\ref{lem:tendsto_M_of_tendsto_charFun}.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Forward direction from bounded continuous test functions; converse via tightness and convergence on the separating algebra of exponential polynomials.

nodes.name: Forward direction
nodes.statement: For all $t$, $x \mapsto e^{i \langle t, x \rangle}$ is a bounded continuous function. Hence by the definition of convergence in distribution, $\mu_n \xrightarrow{w} \mu \implies \hat{\mu}_n(t) \to \hat{\mu}(t)$ for all $t$.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Forward direction: test against bounded continuous exponentials

nodes.name: Converse direction
nodes.statement: Let's now prove the other direction. If the characteristic functions converge pointwise, we get from Lemma~\ref{lem:tight_of_tendsto_charFun} that the family of measures is tight. Then apply Lemma~\ref{lem:cvg_of_separating} to the subalgebra $\mathcal M$: it suffices to show that $\mu_n[f] \to \mu[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal M$. This is obtained with Lemma~\ref{lem:tendsto_M_of_tendsto_charFun}.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Converse direction

nodes.name: Tightness
nodes.statement: If the characteristic functions converge pointwise, we get from Lemma~\ref{lem:tight_of_tendsto_charFun} that the family of measures is tight.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Tightness from Lemma 13

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: Then apply Lemma~\ref{lem:cvg_of_separating} to the subalgebra $\mathcal M$: it suffices to show that $\mu_n[f] \to \mu[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal M$.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to convergence on exponential polynomials

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: This is obtained with Lemma~\ref{lem:tendsto_M_of_tendsto_charFun}.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement_short: Conclude with Lemma 11

nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a real random variable with characteristic function $\phi$, with $\mathbb{E}[\vert X \vert^n] < \infty$. Then as $t \to 0$, \begin{align*} \phi(t) = \sum_{k=0}^n \frac{(it)^k \mathbb{E}[X^k]}{k!} + o(t^n) \: . \end{align*}

as $t \to 0$

nodes.name: Central limit theorem
nodes.statement: Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be i.i.d. real random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, and let $Z$ be a random variable with law $\mathcal N(0,1)$. Then \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{k=1}^n X_k \xrightarrow{d} Z \: . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2.1 The central limit theorem for real random variables
assumptions: Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be i.i.d. real random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, and let $Z$ be a random variable with law $\mathcal N(0,1)$.
nodes.label: thm:clt

nodes.name: Proof of TP2
nodes.statement: Let $S_n = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{k=1}^n X_k$. Let $\phi$ be the characteristic function of $X_k$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:charFun_smul} and~\ref{lem:charFun_add_of_indep}, the characteristic function of $S_n$ is $\phi_n(t) = (\phi(n^{-1/2}t))^n$. By Lemma \ref{lem:charFun_taylor}, \begin{align*} \phi_n(t) = (\phi(n^{-1/2}t))^n = \left(1 - \frac{1}{2n}t^2 + o(\frac{1}{n})\right)^n \to_{n \to +\infty} e^{-t^2/2} \: . \end{align*} Since the r.h.s. is the characteristic function of $Z$, we conclude that $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{k=1}^n X_k \xrightarrow{d} Z$ by Lemma~\ref{thm:charFun_tendsto_iff_measure_tendsto}.
nodes.section: 2.1 The central limit theorem for real random variables
nodes.statement_short: Lévy continuity: the characteristic function of the normalized sum is $(\phi(t/\sqrt n))^n$, which by Taylor expansion tends to $e^{-t^2/2}$.

nodes.name: Introduce S_n, phi
nodes.statement: Let $S_n = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{k=1}^n X_k$. Let $\phi$ be the characteristic function of $X_k$.
nodes.section: 2.1 The central limit theorem for real random variables
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $S_n$ and $\phi$

nodes.name: Char. function of S_n
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:charFun_smul} and~\ref{lem:charFun_add_of_indep}, the characteristic function of $S_n$ is $\phi_n(t) = (\phi(n^{-1/2}t))^n$.
nodes.section: 2.1 The central limit theorem for real random variables
nodes.statement_short: Characteristic function of $S_n$ by scaling and independence

nodes.name: Taylor limit
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:charFun_taylor}, \begin{align*} \phi_n(t) = (\phi(n^{-1/2}t))^n = \left(1 - \frac{1}{2n}t^2 + o(\frac{1}{n})\right)^n \to_{n \to +\infty} e^{-t^2/2} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2.1 The central limit theorem for real random variables
nodes.statement_short: Taylor expansion gives the limit $e^{-t^2/2}$

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since the r.h.s. is the characteristic function of $Z$, we conclude that $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{k=1}^n X_k \xrightarrow{d} Z$ by Lemma~\ref{thm:charFun_tendsto_iff_measure_tendsto}.
nodes.section: 2.1 The central limit theorem for real random variables
nodes.statement_short: Conclude by Lévy's continuity theorem

nodes.name: Cramér-Wold
nodes.statement: Let $X, X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be random variables in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Then $X_n \xrightarrow{d} X$ iff for every $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $\langle a, X_n \rangle \xrightarrow{d} \langle a, X \rangle$.
nodes.section: 2.2 The central limit theorem for random variables in $\mathbb{R}^d$
assumptions: Let $X, X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be random variables in $\mathbb{R}^d$.
conclusions: $X_n \xrightarrow{d} X$ iff for every $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $\langle a, X_n \rangle \xrightarrow{d} \langle a, X \rangle$
equivalent_conditions: for every $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $\langle a, X_n \rangle \xrightarrow{d} \langle a, X \rangle$
nodes.label: thm:cramer_wold

nodes.name: Proof of TP3
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{thm:charFun_tendsto_iff_measure_tendsto}, the convergence in distribution of the random variables is equivalent to the convergence of their characteristic functions for each $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$, which for each such $a$ is equivalent to the convergence in distribution of the random variables $\langle a, X_n \rangle$ by the same theorem.
nodes.section: 2.2 The central limit theorem for random variables in $\mathbb{R}^d$
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lévy's continuity theorem twice: both convergences are equivalent to convergence of characteristic functions along each direction $a$.

nodes.name: Real Gaussian measure
nodes.statement: A measure on $\mathbb{R}$ is Gaussian if it is equal to $\mathcal{N}(m, \sigma^2)$ for some $m \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\sigma^2 \ge 0$, in which $\mathcal{N}(m, \sigma^2)$ is the measure absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure with density $x \mapsto \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi \sigma^2}}e^{- \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}(x - m)^2}$ if $\sigma^2>0$ and the Dirac probability measure at $m$ if $\sigma^2 = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: A measure on $\mathbb{R}$ is Gaussian if it is $\mathcal N(m,\sigma^2)$: the normal density for $\sigma^2>0$, the Dirac mass at $m$ for $\sigma^2=0$.
differentia: it is equal to $\mathcal{N}(m, \sigma^2)$ for some $m \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\sigma^2 \ge 0$
nodes.label: def:gaussianReal

nodes.name: Standard Gaussian on a finite-dimensional space
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be a finite dimensional real inner product space and let $b_1, \ldots, b_d$ be an orthonormal basis of $E$. Let $X_1, \ldots, X_d$ be independent standard Gaussian random variables on $\mathbb{R}$. Then the law of $X_1 b_1 + \ldots + X_d b_d$ is a Gaussian measure on $E$.

nodes.name: Weak convergence of probability measures
nodes.statement: In a topological space $S$ in which the opens are measurable, we say that a sequence of probability measures $\mu_n$ converges weakly to a probability measure $\mu$ and write $\mu_n \xrightarrow{w} \mu$ if $\mu_n[f] \to \mu[f]$ for every bounded continuous function $f : S \to \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mu_n \xrightarrow{w} \mu$ when $\mu_n[f]\to\mu[f]$ for all bounded continuous $f$.
differentia: $\mu_n[f] \to \mu[f]$ for every bounded continuous function $f : S \to \mathbb{R}$
nodes.label: def:weak_cvg_measure

nodes.name: Law of a random variable
nodes.statement: We write $\mathcal L(X)$ for the law of a random variable $X : \Omega \to S$. This is a measure on $S$, defined as the map of the measure on $\Omega$ by $X$.

nodes.name: Convergence in distribution
nodes.statement: We say that $X_n$ converges in distribution to $X$ and write $X_n \xrightarrow{d} X$ if $\mathcal L(X_n) \xrightarrow{w} \mathcal L(X)$.
nodes.label: def:cvg_distribution

nodes.name: Separating points
nodes.statement: A set $\mathcal F$ of functions $E \to F$ separates points in $E$ if for all $x, y \in E$ with $x \ne y$, there exists $f \in \mathcal F$ with $f(x) \ne f(y)$.
nodes.genus: A set $\mathcal F$ of functions $E \to F$
differentia: for all $x, y \in E$ with $x \ne y$, there exists $f \in \mathcal F$ with $f(x) \ne f(y)$
nodes.label: def:separates_points

nodes.name: Proof of LP33
nodes.statement: To show convergence to $\mu$, it suffices to show that every subsequence has a subsequence that converges to $\mu$ (\texttt{Filter.tendsto\_of\_subseq\_tendsto}). Since the family is tight, it is relatively compact by Prokhorov's theorem. We get that each subsequence has a converging subsequence. Let then $\mu'$ be a weak limit of $\mu_n$. We have $\mu_n[f] \to \mu'[f]$ and $\mu_n[f] \to \mu[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal A$, hence $\mu'[f] = \mu[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal A$. Since $\mathcal A$ separates points, $\mathcal \mu' = \mu$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:separating_starSubalgebra}.
nodes.statement_short: Subsequence argument: tightness and Prokhorov give convergent subsequences, and every weak limit agrees with $\mu$ on the separating algebra.

nodes.name: Weak limit
nodes.statement: Let then $\mu'$ be a weak limit of $\mu_n$. We have $\mu_n[f] \to \mu'[f]$ and $\mu_n[f] \to \mu[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal A$, hence $\mu'[f] = \mu[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal A$.
nodes.statement_short: A weak limit agrees with $\mu$ on $\mathcal A$

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal A$ separates points, $\mathcal \mu' = \mu$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:separating_starSubalgebra}.
nodes.statement_short: Separation forces $\mu'=\mu$

nodes.name: Tight set of measures
nodes.statement: A set $S$ of measures on $\Omega$ is tight if for all $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a compact set $K$ such that for all $\mu \in S$, $\mu(K^c) \le \varepsilon$.
differentia: for all $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a compact set $K$ such that for all $\mu \in S$, $\mu(K^c) \le \varepsilon$
nodes.label: def:tight

nodes.name: Tightness via norms
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a set of measures on a finite-dimensional normed space $E$. Then $S$ is tight iff $\lim_{r \to +\infty}\sup_{\mu \in S} \mu\{\Vert x \Vert > r\} = 0$.
assumptions: Let $S$ be a set of measures on a finite-dimensional normed space $E$.
conclusions: $S$ is tight iff $\lim_{r \to +\infty}\sup_{\mu \in S} \mu\{\Vert x \Vert > r\} = 0$
nodes.label: lem:isTightMeasureSet_iff_norm

nodes.name: Tightness via inner products
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a set of measures on a finite-dimensional inner product space $E$. Then $S$ is tight iff for all $y \in E$, $\lim_{r \to +\infty}\sup_{\mu \in S} \mu\{\vert\langle y, x\rangle\vert > r\} = 0$.
assumptions: Let $S$ be a set of measures on a finite-dimensional inner product space $E$.
conclusions: $S$ is tight iff for all $y \in E$, $\lim_{r \to +\infty}\sup_{\mu \in S} \mu\{\vert\langle y, x\rangle\vert > r\} = 0$
equivalent_conditions: for all $y \in E$, $\lim_{r \to +\infty}\sup_{\mu \in S} \mu\{\vert\langle y, x\rangle\vert > r\} = 0$
nodes.label: lem:isTightMeasureSet_iff_sup_inner

nodes.name: Tightness of a sequence via inner products
nodes.statement: Let $(\mu_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of measures on a finite-dimensional inner product space $E$. Then the set $\{\mu_n \mid n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is tight iff for all $y \in E$, $\lim_{r \to +\infty}\limsup_{n \to \infty} \mu_n\{\vert\langle y, x\rangle\vert > r\} = 0$.
assumptions: Let $(\mu_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of measures on a finite-dimensional inner product space $E$.
conclusions: the set $\{\mu_n \mid n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is tight iff for all $y \in E$, $\lim_{r \to +\infty}\limsup_{n \to \infty} \mu_n\{\vert\langle y, x\rangle\vert > r\} = 0$
equivalent_conditions: for all $y \in E$, $\lim_{r \to +\infty}\limsup_{n \to \infty} \mu_n\{\vert\langle y, x\rangle\vert > r\} = 0$
nodes.label: lem:isTightMeasureSet_iff_basis

nodes.name: Prokhorov's theorem
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be a complete separable metric space and let $S \subseteq \mathcal P(E)$. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $S$ is tight. \item the closure of $S$ is compact. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: Let $E$ be a complete separable metric space and let $S \subseteq \mathcal P(E)$.
conclusions: the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $S$ is tight. \item the closure of $S$ is compact. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: thm:prokhorov

nodes.name: Tight sets are relatively compact
